entities.rationale: Extreme water stress, heat and a nuclear-armed rival are the main collapse paths; essentials still cost 31% of income, so near-free needs a large superintelligence-driven jump in wealth and state capacity.
Strong state capacity and low essentials cost make abundance plausible with superintelligence, but a Taiwan war and extreme aging are the key risks.

Wealth and likely leadership in AI favour abundance if superintelligence arrives, but health spending alone is about 17% of GDP, so near-free is very hard without it; polarisation and great-power war are the main collapse risks.
Relatively peaceful with energy self-sufficiency, but very low safe-water coverage and middle income keep abundance unlikely; sea-level rise and political instability are the main threats.
Very low political stability, severe water stress, climate exposure and nuclear rivalry with India make a breakdown of security or water a real risk; low income makes near-free essentials remote.
Insurgencies, weak governance, high hunger and fast population growth drive collapse risk mainly through security and food; essentials already cost 38% of income.
Food and energy surpluses and low water stress make collapse fairly unlikely, but high violence, debt and middle income hold back abundance.
A low delta with high climate vulnerability and weak readiness to adapt faces sea-level rise, flooding and salinity that threaten water and food; strong health gains are the bright spot.
Ongoing war, a brittle regime and nuclear escalation risk make security the main collapse path; energy and food surpluses help, but weak governance limits abundance.
Recurring civil war, famine history and very low income make security and food breakdowns likely risks; abundance needs both peace and a transformative technology shock.
Cartel violence and very high water stress are the main threats; ties to the US economy could spread superintelligence gains, but low safe-water coverage and insecurity hold back abundance.
Excellent governance and safety favour abundance with superintelligence, but heavy energy and food imports, extreme aging and regional war risk are the vulnerabilities.
Near-total dependence on the Nile, extreme water stress, food imports and a heavy debt burden make water and food the main collapse paths; cheap desalination from superintelligence could change that.
Typhoons, sea-level rise and South China Sea tensions are the main risks; low safe-water coverage and import dependence keep abundance unlikely.
Chronic war, the weakest governance in the set and 40% undernourishment make a nationwide security or food collapse likely over 75 years; abundance is very remote.
Stable, low-debt and fast-growing, but the Mekong delta faces sea-level rise and salinity, and tension with China is a security risk.
Water depletion is already acute and political instability, sanctions and war with Israel and the US are real risks; good health and energy reserves are the strengths.
Fairly high income, low debt and good health help, but rising water stress, energy imports, earthquakes and a volatile region are the main risks.
Strong institutions and wealth make local collapse unlikely and abundance plausible with superintelligence; without it, aging-driven health costs keep the essentials well above 10% of income.
A food exporter with good health outcomes, but high water stress, a sinking Bangkok, energy imports and recurring coups are the main vulnerabilities.
